05 · Model Interpretation & Error Analysis¶

A prediction is only useful in a clinical context if we can explain it. This notebook opens up the final models from notebook 04:

  1. Permutation importance (model-agnostic, on the test set)
  2. SHAP values: global summary + individual explanations
  3. Partial-dependence & ICE curves
  4. Odds ratios from the transparent logistic model
  5. Error analysis: who does the model get wrong?
  6. Applying the model to the unlabelled Brown site
In [13]:
import sys, json, warnings
from pathlib import Path
sys.path.insert(0, str(Path.cwd().parent / "src"))
warnings.filterwarnings("ignore")

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
import joblib, shap
from sklearn.inspection import permutation_importance, PartialDependenceDisplay

from neuroadhd.config import DATA_PROCESSED, MODELS, REPORTS, WEBSITE_DATA, RANDOM_STATE
from neuroadhd.data import load_clean
from neuroadhd.features import FEATURE_SETS, add_features
from neuroadhd.plotting import savefig, PALETTE, TD_COLOR, ADHD_COLOR, DIVERGING, INK, INK_2, MUTED, SURFACE

df = pd.read_csv(DATA_PROCESSED / "adhd200_model_ready.csv")
results = json.loads((REPORTS / "model_results.json").read_text())
models = {s: joblib.load(MODELS / f"best_model_{s}.joblib") for s in FEATURE_SETS}
LABELS = {"A_demographic_cognitive": "Set A", "B_with_symptom_ratings": "Set B"}

def split(s, part):
    d = df[df.split == part]
    if s.startswith("B"): d = d[d.rating_scale.notna()]
    return d, d[FEATURE_SETS[s]["numeric"]], d["adhd"].values

for s in FEATURE_SETS:
    print(f"{LABELS[s]}: {results['test'][s]['model']}  test AUC={results['test'][s]['roc_auc']:.3f}")

Set A: Random Forest  test AUC=0.729
Set B: Logistic Regression  test AUC=0.955

1. Permutation importance¶

How much does test ROC-AUC drop when one feature is randomly shuffled? (20 repeats)

In [14]:
perm = {}
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(16, 5.2))
for ax, s in zip(axes, FEATURE_SETS):
    _, Xt, yt = split(s, "test")
    r = permutation_importance(models[s], Xt, yt, scoring="roc_auc", n_repeats=20, random_state=RANDOM_STATE, n_jobs=-1)
    imp = pd.DataFrame({"feature": Xt.columns, "mean": r.importances_mean, "sd": r.importances_std}).sort_values("mean")
    perm[s] = imp
    ax.barh(imp.feature, imp["mean"], xerr=imp["sd"], color=[ADHD_COLOR if v == imp["mean"].max() else PALETTE[0] for v in imp["mean"]],
            height=0.62, error_kw={"ecolor": MUTED, "lw": 1})
    ax.axvline(0, color=INK_2, lw=0.8); ax.grid(axis="y", visible=False)
    ax.set_xlabel("drop in test ROC-AUC when shuffled"); ax.set_title(f"{LABELS[s]} · {results['test'][s]['model']}")
fig.suptitle("Permutation importance", x=0.01, ha="left", fontsize=13.5, fontweight="semibold")
fig.tight_layout(); savefig(fig, "05_permutation_importance"); plt.show()

2. SHAP values¶

SHAP splits each individual prediction into additive contributions per feature. A model-agnostic permutation explainer is used, so it works with any final model (including ensembles), with training data as background.

In [15]:
shap_vals = {}
for s in FEATURE_SETS:
    _, Xtr, _ = split(s, "train"); _, Xt, _ = split(s, "test")
    cols = list(Xt.columns)
    f = lambda X, m=models[s], c=cols: m.predict_proba(pd.DataFrame(X, columns=c))[:, 1]
    background = Xtr.fillna(Xtr.median()).sample(100, random_state=RANDOM_STATE)
    explainer = shap.Explainer(f, background, feature_names=cols, algorithm="permutation", seed=RANDOM_STATE)
    shap_vals[s] = explainer(Xt.fillna(Xtr.median()), max_evals=2 * len(cols) + 1, silent=True)
    print(s, shap_vals[s].values.shape)

A_demographic_cognitive (187, 9)
B_with_symptom_ratings (98, 13)
In [16]:
for s in FEATURE_SETS:
    plt.figure()
    shap.plots.beeswarm(shap_vals[s], max_display=14, show=False, color=plt.get_cmap(DIVERGING), plot_size=(11, 5.2))
    fig = plt.gcf(); fig.axes[0].set_title(f"SHAP summary · {LABELS[s]} ({results['test'][s]['model']})", loc="left", fontsize=13, fontweight="semibold")
    fig.axes[0].set_xlabel("SHAP value (impact on predicted ADHD probability)")
    savefig(fig, f"05_shap_beeswarm_{LABELS[s].replace(' ', '')}"); plt.show()

How to read it: each dot is one test child. Dots right of zero push the prediction toward ADHD; colour shows the feature value (red = high, blue = low).

  • Set A: being male and having lower IQ (especially performance IQ) push toward ADHD; age has a non-linear effect.
  • Set B: the ADHD index / inattention severity dominate; demographics barely matter once symptoms are known.

⚠️ A hidden site artefact: handedness. It ranks second in Set A, but not because left-handedness causes ADHD. NYU (58 % ADHD) records a continuous laterality index, so 87 % of NYU children have values below 1, while every other site mostly records the word "Right" (= 1, at most 12 % below 1). "Handedness < 1" therefore partly means "scanned at NYU". Explainability tools catch confounds that accuracy numbers hide.

In [17]:
s = "A_demographic_cognitive"
dt, Xt, yt = split(s, "test")
proba = models[s].predict_proba(Xt)[:, 1]
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(16, 5))
for ax, idx, title in [(axes[0], int(np.argmax(np.where(yt == 1, proba, -1))), "Most confident ADHD prediction"),
                       (axes[1], int(np.argmin(np.where(yt == 0, proba, 2))), "Most confident TD prediction")]:
    sv = shap_vals[s][idx]
    order = np.argsort(np.abs(sv.values))
    vals = sv.values[order]; names = [f"{n} = {v:.3g}" if not np.isnan(v) else f"{n} = n/a" for n, v in zip(np.array(sv.feature_names)[order], Xt.iloc[idx].values[order])]
    ax.barh(names, vals, color=[ADHD_COLOR if v > 0 else TD_COLOR for v in vals], height=0.62)
    ax.axvline(0, color=INK_2, lw=0.8); ax.grid(axis="y", visible=False)
    ax.set_title(f"{title}\nbase {sv.base_values:.2f} → predicted {proba[idx]:.2f}  (true: {'ADHD' if yt[idx] else 'TD'})", fontsize=11.5)
    ax.set_xlabel("SHAP contribution")
fig.tight_layout(); savefig(fig, "05_shap_individual"); plt.show()

3. Partial dependence & ICE (Set A)¶

The average effect of a feature (thick line) and each child's individual curve (thin lines).

In [18]:
s = "A_demographic_cognitive"
_, Xtr, _ = split(s, "train")
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(17, 4.6))
PartialDependenceDisplay.from_estimator(models[s], Xtr, ["age", "performance_iq", "verbal_iq"], kind="both", subsample=120,
                                        random_state=RANDOM_STATE, ax=axes, n_jobs=-1,
                                        ice_lines_kw={"color": PALETTE[0], "alpha": 0.12, "lw": 0.8},
                                        pd_line_kw={"color": ADHD_COLOR, "lw": 3})
for ax in fig.axes:
    if ax.get_legend(): ax.get_legend().remove()
fig.suptitle("Partial dependence (orange) and ICE curves (blue) · Set A", x=0.01, ha="left", fontsize=13, fontweight="semibold")
fig.tight_layout(); savefig(fig, "05_partial_dependence"); plt.show()

4. Odds ratios from the transparent logistic model¶

The logistic model used by the website's interactive demo. Odds ratio per 1 standard deviation increase.

In [19]:
demo = json.loads((WEBSITE_DATA / "demo_model.json").read_text())
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(16, 5))
for ax, s in zip(axes, FEATURE_SETS):
    o = pd.DataFrame({"feature": demo[s]["features"], "OR": np.exp(demo[s]["coef"])}).sort_values("OR")
    ax.barh(o.feature, o.OR - 1, left=1, color=[ADHD_COLOR if v > 1 else TD_COLOR for v in o.OR], height=0.62)
    ax.axvline(1, color=INK_2, lw=0.8); ax.set_xscale("log"); ax.grid(axis="y", visible=False)
    ax.set_xlabel("odds ratio per +1 SD (log scale)"); ax.set_title(f"{LABELS[s]} · logistic regression (CV AUC {demo[s]['cv_auc']:.3f})")
fig.tight_layout(); savefig(fig, "05_odds_ratios"); plt.show()

5. Error analysis (Set A)¶

In [20]:
s = "A_demographic_cognitive"
dt, Xt, yt = split(s, "test")
thr = results["test"][s]["threshold"]
p = models[s].predict_proba(Xt)[:, 1]
ea = dt.assign(prob=p, pred=(p >= thr).astype(int))
ea["outcome"] = np.select([(ea.adhd == 1) & (ea.pred == 1), (ea.adhd == 0) & (ea.pred == 0), (ea.adhd == 0) & (ea.pred == 1)],
                          ["True positive", "True negative", "False positive"], "False negative")
ea.groupby("outcome")[["age", "sex_male", "full_iq", "verbal_iq", "performance_iq"]].mean().round(2).assign(n=ea.outcome.value_counts())

In [21]:
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(15, 4.6))
ax = axes[0]
for g, c, lab in [(0, TD_COLOR, "TD"), (1, ADHD_COLOR, "ADHD")]:
    ax.hist(ea.loc[ea.adhd == g, "prob"], bins=np.linspace(0, 1, 21), color=c, alpha=0.6, label=lab, edgecolor=SURFACE)
ax.axvline(thr, color=INK, ls="--", lw=1.2); ax.text(thr + 0.01, ax.get_ylim()[1] * 0.92, f"threshold {thr:.2f}", fontsize=9, color=INK_2)
ax.set_xlabel("predicted ADHD probability"); ax.set_ylabel("test children"); ax.legend(); ax.set_title("Score distribution by true diagnosis")
ax = axes[1]
err = ea.groupby("site").apply(lambda g: (g.adhd != g.pred).mean(), include_groups=False).sort_values()
ax.barh(err.index, err.values * 100, color=PALETTE[0], height=0.6)
for i, v in enumerate(err.values): ax.text(v * 100 + 1, i, f"{v:.0%}", va="center", fontsize=9, color=INK_2)
ax.set_xlabel("% misclassified"); ax.grid(axis="y", visible=False); ax.set_xlim(0, max(err.values) * 100 + 12)
ax.set_title("Error rate by site (test set)")
fig.tight_layout(); savefig(fig, "05_error_analysis"); plt.show()

Findings

  • False negatives are mostly ADHD children with average or high IQ and girls: the model's two strongest cues point the wrong way for them.
  • False positives are mostly TD boys with below-average IQ.
  • Error rates vary by site, consistent with the leave-one-site-out results.

6. Predicting the unlabelled Brown site¶

Brown's diagnoses were never released, so this shows how the Set A model would be used on new, unlabelled children.

In [22]:
brown = add_features(pd.read_csv(DATA_PROCESSED / "adhd200_unlabelled.csv"))
pb = models["A_demographic_cognitive"].predict_proba(brown[FEATURE_SETS["A_demographic_cognitive"]["numeric"]])[:, 1]
brown_out = brown[["subject_key", "age", "sex_male", "full_iq"]].assign(adhd_probability=pb.round(3),
            predicted=np.where(pb >= results["test"]["A_demographic_cognitive"]["threshold"], "ADHD", "TD"))
brown_out.to_csv(REPORTS / "brown_predictions.csv", index=False)
print(brown_out.predicted.value_counts().to_string())
brown_out.sort_values("adhd_probability", ascending=False).head(10)

saved

Summary¶

  • Without questionnaires, the model relies on sex and IQ: real but weak population-level signals that cannot diagnose an individual child. It also exploits a handedness-coding artefact linked to site.
  • With questionnaires, the parent-rated ADHD index decides almost everything.
  • Errors concentrate in groups that do not match the "typical" profile (girls, high-IQ children), a reminder that ML can encode existing diagnostic biases.
